## SCORE in brief {#score-in-brief .smaller}

::: {.fs-80}
| Repetition | The study | What came back |
|:-----|:-----|:-----|
| **Reproduction** – same data, same analysis | The SCORE reproducibility study: 600 papers from 62 journals, 2009–2018 [@MiskeEtAl2026InvestigatingReproducibilitySocial] | Of the 143 that could be assessed, **53.6%** reproduced precisely and **73.5%** at least approximately; counting the papers that nobody could check, about **18%** |
| **Robustness** – same data, other analyses | The SCORE robustness study: 100 studies, at least 5 analysts each [@AczelEtAl2026InvestigatingAnalyticalRobustness] | **74%** of reanalyses reached the same conclusion; **34%** came within ±0.05 *d* of the original effect size |
| **Replication** – new data | The SCORE replicability study: 274 claims, independent data [@TynerEtAl2026InvestigatingReplicabilitySocial] | **55.1%** significant again; the median effect size fell from *r* = 0.25 to 0.10 |
:::

::: {.fragment .small}
Measured on the same body of papers, the three are **essentially uncorrelated**: knowing how a finding fared on one tells you almost nothing about the others.
:::

::: notes
SCORE, a programme funded by DARPA, the research agency of the US Department of Defense, put the central claims of a sample of social-science papers through each of the three repetitions on the grid. In the reproducibility study, of the hundred and forty-three papers that could be assessed, about half reproduced precisely and three quarters at least approximately, but counted against all six hundred papers, most of which nobody could check, the rate is about eighteen per cent. In the robustness study, three quarters of the reanalyses reached the same conclusion as the original, while only a third came close to its effect size. In the replicability study, fifty-five per cent of the claims were significant again on new data, with the median effect size more than halved. [advance] Across the same papers the three outcomes barely predict one another, so for any one paper we have to ask which of the three it passed.
:::
